title: Choose the visual world
question: Choose the visual direction for the WeekToDoOnline redesign.

options.label: The Quiet Time Ledger
options.lineage: Personal time-block ledgers and focus journals
options.thesis: A calm working ledger that makes the whole week legible without demanding attention.
options.viewport: The current week is one continuous ledger: days as columns, morning-to-night bands as rows, and completed work visibly settling into place.
options.risk: Can feel too quiet if completion states lack enough contrast and warmth.

options.label: The Gentle Weekly Grid
options.lineage: Accessible editorial calendars and classroom week boards
options.thesis: A generous grid that turns the week into a dependable visual map.
options.viewport: A seven-day overview with a strong today rail, four day-part bands, and completed tasks compressed but still readable.
options.risk: Seven columns can become cramped on small screens without a decisive mobile transformation.

options.label: The Human Timetable
options.lineage: Wayfinding timetables and dependable transit boards
options.thesis: The week behaves like a reliable timetable: clear departures, arrivals, and status at a glance.
options.viewport: Today anchors the screen; each day-part is a departure band with explicit current, next, and done states.
options.risk: Status language could feel institutional if the copy is not humane.

options.label: The Library Card Catalog
options.lineage: Library cards and quiet reference rooms
options.thesis: Every task is a small reference card, organized so the mind can find its place.
options.viewport: The week is a shelf of day cards; opening a day reveals its four day-part drawers and a concise done archive.
options.risk: Card metaphors can add interaction steps where quick capture matters.

options.label: The Focus Garden
options.lineage: Japanese dry gardens and deliberate negative space
options.thesis: The week is arranged as a few intentional zones, with empty space doing useful work.
options.viewport: A quiet weekly landscape with one active day, four temporal zones, and completed tasks receding into a low-noise margin.
options.risk: Too metaphorical could reduce the concrete task clarity this audience needs.

options.label: The Monospace Notebook
options.thesis: A precise text-first planner where structure, not decoration, carries the experience.
options.viewport: A readable week outline with indentation for day-parts and compact inline completion states.
options.risk: Can underserve users who need stronger visual grouping and orientation.

options.label: The category standard
options.thesis: A conventional modern calendar interface, executed with exceptional clarity.
options.viewport: A standard weekly calendar with a clear today highlight, day-part sections, and visible task completion.
options.risk: Familiar and effective, but less distinctive and easier to make visually busy.
